summary.text: 记 means “record” or “remember.” Its traditional form 記 combines 言, marking a speech-and-words category, with 己 as a sound component.

formation.text: 記 is analyzed as a phonosemantic compound: 言 contributes a meaning category, while 己 supplies a sound cue. This is the received early dictionary analysis, not independent proof of the character’s original formation. 记 is the simplified form of 記.

components.text: In 記, 言 marks the speech-and-words category. In 记, its conventional side form is 讠; the detailed graphic path in this character is not established.
In 記, 己 supplies the sound cue. Its earliest referent as a standalone character remains unsettled; that is separate from its role here.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, 記 is reconstructed as *kɯs and 己 as *kɯʔ. They share an initial and rhyme, though their endings differ.

history.text: The received Shuowen entry analyzes 記 as 言 with 己 as its sound component and gives the gloss 疏也. A later commentary explains the gloss in terms of distinguishing and recognizing items; another edition reads 疋也.
記 is represented in bronze, small-seal, and clerical script traditions. These examples do not establish exact dates, a continuous sequence, or the earliest attestation.
记 is identified as simplified from 記. The date and detailed graphic path, including the change from 言 to 讠 in this character, are not established.

uncertainties.text: The received gloss 疏也 has a variant reading 疋也. Its relationship to later “record” and “remember” senses is unclear, as are the chronology of those senses and the exact earliest attestation.
The earliest referent of standalone 己 remains unsettled; this does not alter its phonetic role in the received analysis of 記.
The date and detailed graphic steps from 言 to 讠 in 记 are not established.

Etymological analysis: 己 (phonetic)

The Eastern Han dictionary entry glosses 記 as 疏也 and analyzes it as 从言己聲: 言 is the semantic element and 己 the phonetic element, according to Xu Shen. This is an early historical analysis, not independent proof of the original meaning or component history.
